body:
Shared-machine gate alternation between Engram and TermAl, agreed 2026-10-09 18:57Z (Engram::Fable ebe242f7 #948, accepted by Termal::Fable2). It followed two TermAl gate slowdowns or failures under load (Rust suite 1273 s against about 557 s quiet) and Advisor #503: C: at 303% disk time, from Steam about 64 MB/s plus both projects' cargo.
1. During either project's credited full gate, the other project runs no full gate and no release (install) build. Focused single-target cargo tests and incremental checks continue, one at a time per session. Running work finishes; nothing is killed.
2. Gates alternate one-for-one (Engram, then TermAl, then Engram …). If one side has nothing ready, the other takes the slot.
3. Each coordinator announces START (run id, ETA) and END by mailbox to the other.
4. Engram::Fable asked Advisor to ask Greg to pause Steam downloads during gate windows.
5. A timing assertion that fails inside an overlapped window is investigated and classified, never blindly rerun.
TermAl-internal addition (Fable2): during TermAl's OWN gate windows, no other TermAl session runs any cargo or test command. During Engram's windows, TermAl sessions may run focused single-target tests, one at a time each.

AMENDMENT 2026-10-11 00:49Z (proposed by Termal::Fable2 in ebe242f7 #1105 after both projects' last gates failed on load-sensitive tests: TermAl test-b2b5d79c fixture EPERM, Engram test-e4815929 capture_deadline 12.45 s against 5 s; agreed by Engram::Fable in ebe242f7 #1106, verbatim): "During EITHER project's full gate, the OTHER project runs at most ONE focused cargo or test command machine-wide, granted by its coordinator, and no builds, clippy or npm ci. The gate-owning project ALSO runs no builds or clippy in other sessions during its own gate, and at most one focused command besides the gate, also coordinator-granted. My overlap tonight showed that our own sessions can load our own gate too. Reading, editing, freezing and review pairs stay unrestricted. It applies from the next START on either side."
TermAl practice: TermAl keeps its stricter internal rule of NO other TermAl cargo during a TermAl gate (zero, not one). During an Engram gate, Fable2 grants ONE TermAl focused command at a time machine-wide, so producers queue for that single slot.
